program: Community air monitoring and clean-air policy advocacy
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Air Alliance Houston researches air pollution and supports communities exposed to industrial and transport emissions.
It monitors local air and helps residents engage with permits, regulators and public planning.
Its campaigns seek cleaner air and stronger protections for Houston-area neighborhoods.
strengths: Current reporting identifies named local permit and monitoring mechanisms with coalition partners.
Original finance separates advocacy and research costs from wider recipient work.
Primary quasi-experimental pollution evidence supports potential health and work channels when pollution actually changes.
reservations: Sensors, notifications and permit holds do not establish attributable sustained pollution reduction.
Potential benefit residents are not automatically advocates bearing process costs; participation is separately judged.
Local dose, net resources, implementation probability, displacement and gift-driven expansion remain unknown.

sections.what: Air Alliance Houston researches air pollution and supports communities exposed to industrial and transport emissions. It monitors local air and helps residents engage with permits, regulators and public planning. Its campaigns seek cleaner air and stronger protections for Houston-area neighborhoods.
sections.monitoring: FY 2025 reports 56,519 AirMail households across 12 permits, two concrete facilities on hold and over 70 sensors across 14 neighborhoods; current September 2026 monitoring 100+sensors/10 communities uses a later scope. Neither sensors nor households notified establish unique health beneficiaries. Current report explicitly explains ozone patterns through weather and maintenance, not recipient causality. Its cleaner metal-recycler anecdote after a press event is not a controlled measured emissions change. The cancelled EPA grant cannot be delivered capacity. The October 2025 Julpit recipient statement describes a voided permit and homes nearby, not permanent prevention; the current updates index includes reapplication. Request permit conditions, actual enforcement/operations dates, pollutant-specific exposure before/after versus weather and alternative regulation, active participant households, net household resources and displaced worker/provider incidence.
sections.qualitative: Current campaigns name port partners, industrial permits and transport mechanisms. Original Chay/Greenstone Clean Air Act research uses regulatory nonattainment variation to study infant mortality; this supports an implemented-pollution health mechanism, not a generic adult QALY coefficient or AAH attribution. Original Hanna/Oliva author-hosted refinery-closure study examines actual pollution changes and labor hours with neighborhood comparisons; it is not local after-tax income, does not make every resident employed and cannot import gross wages or closure effects into advocacy. Reading focused on its abstract/introduction and identification discussion, not all 58 pages. No national population or mortality statistic is multiplied into a local impact claim. Cleaner air can improve health and work, while compliance, product prices or displaced employment can offset net resources. Implementation, pollutant dose, alternative regulator/industry action and recipient causal share remain explicit uncertainties.
sections.cost: Initial $21.37 M per better life is preserved: health 1.147147 plus income .067097. Revised conditional reference $20.56 M combines health 1.165056 and signed resources .096914 =1.261970 equivalent years against $2,594,790. This modest change separates the engagement population and joint resource incidence; it is not a measured effectiveness improvement. The original policy factor .3 enactment*.5 implementation*.2 recipient attribution=.03 is retained judgment, with 10,000 potential resident opportunities,150 clinical responders, q.003 for 3 finite years after 2-year delay and .95 local share. These are not sensor, permit or trial coefficients. A separate illustrative 100 engaged household-consumption proxies, not observed 100 unique bus-attendee households, bear full $10 process/time and .0001 stress harm independent of b. Assumed random overlap splits 150 resource-success proxies into 1.5 engaged and 148.5 not-engaged;98.5 unsuccessful engaged proxies retain full costs. Each overlapping household has one joint log, not averaged $0.10 cost applied to all 10,000;100/300/1000/full-resident burdens are distinct sensitivity regimes. $100 otherwise-paid medical/foregone-work resource hypothesis, success.5 and positive-only overlap.5 yield 50 net positive resources before full participant costs, not healthcare retail price or duplicated clinical welfare. Unknown workgain zero is not evidence no income benefit; positive and negative cases are explicit. Distinct displaced workers are separate assumed people whose losses occur conditional on additional implemented policy b, not on failed policy. External payer/compliance incidence is localized once; negative costs are never removed by positive overlap. Actual b 0 leaves advocacy effort burdens; N 0 with burdenN 0 means no exposure and is different. Full annual recipient cost includes other channels not modeled. Advocacy+research recognized $558,209 sensitivity gives $4.42 M, excluding overhead, fundraising and regulator/industry resources and not establishing a single campaign cost; all-program $2,082,550 is also broader than the channel. Whole portfolio EV and marginal gift response remain unknown.
sections.funding: The latest original return covers July 2024–June 2025: $2,588,981 of functional expenses plus $5,809 of direct event expenses netted from revenue gives $2,594,790. The years ending June 2024 and June 2023 report $3,200,249 and $2,785,438, with unpopulated direct-event expense lines. FY 2025 education expense of $1,524,341 and air-quality advocacy expense of $180,396 are activity costs, not measured health returns. The annual report records the cancellation of an EPA grant; its intended funding cannot be counted as delivered capacity. The conditional benefits are finite future effects attributed to one annual work hypothesis, not perpetual policy credit. Original advocacy $180,396 plus research $377,813 = $558,209; these cannot be assigned wholesale to one permit campaign. Total program expense $2,082,550 is an additional partial numerator, not full resources. Current funding loss and coalition/public baseline prevent an automatic proportional next-gift claim.

model.costScope: Full annual recognized recipient expense against hypothetical single implemented local permit/mitigation channel; other campaign, education and monitoring benefits unknown, not zero. Not complete portfolio EV or marginal donation.
model.geographicAttribution: Houston metro-focused campaign envelope; N10,000 potential residents and .95 local share are judgments, not sensor or AirMail beneficiary counts. No national regulatory benefits credited.
model.formula: Potential residents=N*unique; incremental policy benefit union=N*unique*b (.3 enactment*.5 implementation*.2 recipient attribution). Clinical=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite years minus independent engaged-population process harms. Joint resource logs partition changed engaged, changed non-engaged and unchanged engaged households; costs stay full for actual engaged cohort even b0. Distinct payer losses localized once; displaced worker losses conditional on additional implementation b. Headline=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.attribution: Separates enactment .3, implementation .5, recipient attribution .2 against regulator/industry/coalition alternatives; multiplicative .03 is explicit judgment, not estimated local success frequency. Participant effort burdens have their own population, not policy-success probability.
model.uncertainty: Implemented local emissions/dose and population remain unverified; causal pollution studies inform mechanisms, not local QALYs, income or recipient attribution. Participation overlap, net resources, compliance/displacement and marginal capacity are uncertain.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional implemented emissions reduction and actual exposure change, not sensors, households mailed, testimony, permit hold or grant award.

inputs.name: displacedPeople
inputs.unit: distinct workers affected if additional policy implemented
inputs.rationale: Zero unknown-neutral; distinct50-worker adverse case multiplied by policy b, not claimed observed job loss or unconditional failure burden.

inputs.name: displacedGain
inputs.unit: USD annual net disposable resource change per displaced worker
inputs.rationale: After alternative employment, taxes/benefits and replacement income; −1000 adverse scenario judgment, not gross salary loss.

inputs.name: clinicalN
inputs.rationale: Same resident envelope as resource opportunities; not added to it or actual diagnoses.

inputs.name: clinicalResponse
inputs.unit: clinically benefiting share of incremental resident envelope
inputs.rationale: Unmeasured local pollution-dose response, distinct from enactment/implementation/attribution; not imported infant mortality or labor elasticity.
